jest_testing_playbook.overview: Comprehensive Jest testing patterns and best practices for TypeScript and JavaScript projects. Covers test structure, the full matcher catalog, async testing, mocking strategies, data-driven tests, error handling, snapshot testing, anti-patterns, CI/CD integration, and debugging. Optimized for AI agents writing production-quality tests.

test_structure.rule: Use describe() blocks for logical grouping by component, class, or module.
Use test() or it() for individual test cases with descriptive names.
Include setup/teardown hooks (beforeEach, afterEach) for consistent state.
Follow AAA pattern: Arrange (set up data and mocks), Act (call the function), Assert (verify the result).

forbidden_patterns.note: These should never appear in committed test code.
forbidden_patterns.pattern: it.only / test.only / describe.only — prevents other tests from running
it.skip / test.skip / describe.skip / it.todo — dead test code
Empty test bodies without assertions — false sense of coverage
Tests without proper async handling — can silently pass
Hardcoded timeouts or delays (setTimeout in tests) — use fake timers
Tests depending on external services without mocks — fragile and slow

matcher.note: Use for exact type matching. Does NOT work for deep object comparison.

matcher.use_case: Exact object matching including undefined properties
matcher.note: Enforces complete type conformity. Preferred for strict validation.

matcher.use_case: Partial string match in expect helpers
Object has property with optional value
Nested object matching in expect helpers
Match any value of a given constructor

best_practices.rule: Always use expect.assertions(n) or expect.hasAssertions() for async tests — prevents false positives when promises silently resolve.
Prefer async/await over Promise chains for readability.
Use .resolves and .rejects for concise Promise testing.
Wrap done() callback assertions in try/catch blocks to surface failures.

pattern.note: Legacy pattern — prefer async/await when possible.
pattern.warning: Always wrap assertions in try/catch with done() callback. Without try/catch, a failing assertion causes an unhelpful timeout error instead of showing the actual failure.

assertion_counting.method: expect.assertions(3) — exactly 3 assertions must be called in this test.
expect.hasAssertions() — at least 1 assertion must be called.
beforeEach(expect.hasAssertions) — apply to all tests in the describe block.

creation.method: jest.fn() — creates a basic mock function with no implementation.
jest.fn(implementation) — creates a mock with a specific implementation.
jest.fn().mockName('fetchUser') — named mock for better error messages and debugging.

assertions.matcher: Function was called at least once.
Nth call used specific arguments: expect(fn).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, 'arg')

pattern.note: Not hoisted — useful for per-test mocking.

manual_mocks.rule: Place mock file at __mocks__/module-name.js (adjacent to node_modules for npm packages, adjacent to the module for local files).
Call jest.mock('module-name') to activate — Jest automatically uses the __mocks__ file.

cleanup.note: Always clean up mocks to prevent cross-test contamination.

individual.method: mockFn.mockClear() — clears call history (mock.calls, mock.results) but keeps implementation.
mockFn.mockReset() — clears history AND removes implementation (returns undefined).
mockFn.mockRestore() — restores original implementation. Only works on jest.spyOn mocks.

global.method: jest.clearAllMocks() — clear all mock call history.

timer_mocking.setup: jest.useFakeTimers() — replaces setTimeout, setInterval, Date.now with controllable fakes.

methods.method: jest.runAllTimers() — execute all pending timers immediately.
jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms) — advance timers by specific milliseconds.
jest.runOnlyPendingTimers() — run only currently pending timers (not newly created ones).

timer_mocking.cleanup_note: Call jest.useRealTimers() in afterEach if only some tests need fake timers.

pattern.description: Parameterized tests with array of arrays.
Tagged template literal syntax — more readable for complex data sets.
Parameterized describe blocks for testing across contexts.

mock_typing.pattern: const mockFn = jest.fn() as jest.MockedFunction<typeof originalFn>
const mockModule = jest.mocked(originalModule) — preferred in Jest 29+, infers types automatically.
const spy = jest.spyOn(object, 'method') as jest.SpyInstance<ReturnType, Parameters>

pattern.note: Use when you need to inspect the error object beyond the message.
Use for objects with dynamic values like IDs or timestamps.

patterns.pattern: expect(value).toMatchInlineSnapshot() — Jest writes the snapshot inline in the test file.

best_practices.rule: Use property matchers for dynamic values (IDs, timestamps, random data).
Keep snapshots small and focused — snapshot a specific output, not an entire component tree.
Review snapshot changes carefully in code review — they are easy to blindly update.
Avoid snapshots for volatile data that changes frequently.

anti_patterns.note: Common mistakes that lead to fragile, misleading, or unreliable tests.

anti_pattern.description: Testing implementation details instead of behavior.
anti_pattern.reason: Implementation can change without changing behavior. Test what the user sees or what the API returns.

anti_pattern.description: Not cleaning up mocks between tests.
anti_pattern.bad: // No afterEach cleanup — mock state leaks between tests
anti_pattern.reason: Leaked mock state causes flaky tests that pass in isolation but fail when run together.
Real timers make tests slow and timing-dependent. Fake timers are deterministic and instant.

anti_pattern.description: Not awaiting async operations in tests.
anti_pattern.good: test('async', async () => { const result = await asyncFn(); expect(result).toBe(true); })
anti_pattern.reason: Without await, the test completes before the async operation finishes — assertions never run, test always passes.

quality_gates.gate: No .only or .skip tests in committed code.
All async tests must have assertion counts (expect.assertions or expect.hasAssertions).
No console.log statements in test files.

test_debugging.tip: Use --verbose flag for detailed test output showing each test name and status.
Use --detectOpenHandles to find async operations that prevent Jest from exiting cleanly.
Run a single test with --testNamePattern='pattern' to isolate failures.
Run a single file with jest path/to/test.ts to narrow scope.
Add temporary console.log statements, but remove before committing.

mock_debugging.tip: Use .mockName('descriptiveName') for better error messages when mock assertions fail.
Inspect mock.calls array to see exact arguments for each call: console.log(mockFn.mock.calls)
Inspect mock.results array to see return values: console.log(mockFn.mock.results)
Use toMatchSnapshot() on mock.calls for complex call verification during development.
